Messages.Author: Derek Ray
Messages.Body:
So I see there's a whole bunch of bullshit been posted lately that vote
decks are dead and not worth playing. Allow me to just laugh in all
your faces, openly, and predict that vote decks will get NO WEAKER as a
result of this change, because the stuff that made them good has nothing
at all to do with DU/KR.

The primary arguments I've seen are these:

-- Vote decks are weakened because they can't "get away" from a hostile
Rush predator or prey.

Well, suck it up and adapt, nerd-boys, because you're in the same boat
as any NON-vote deck now. Those decks couldn't "get away" either, and
they seem to be doing just fine against the myth of bad seating* -- you
will learn to do the same, or you will just accept that you're no longer
a "good" player. One way or the other, it's your choice.

The cards would have been fine if your decision to bail affected you
alone; ie "I bail out", and it only affected the deck you were bailing
out or getting away from. But the vast, VAST majority of the time (and
you KNOW that's true, bitches, so don't even try to whine to me about
it) that's not how the vote was used; it was used to get behind the
person who was low on pool and/or defenseless. If it was Kindred
Restructure, you got the added benefit of being able to put the person
you could most easily defend against as your predator.

-- Vote decks will have to include all KRC and there won't be any
variety, which is bad.

There are plenty of other vote cards besides KRC. I'm sure all you
clever souls who focus on variety at the expense of winning can figure
out what to throw in. But honestly, variety isn't what the tournament
rules are based on. The tournament rules assume that players will build
decks that try to win, not decks that try to look cool in shades.

The offensive power behind vote decks has always been the triple-threat
of KRC, Parity Shift, and Domain Challenge. Replace with Con Ag if
you're _really_ worried about Delaying Tactics, add some Ancilla
Empowerment to help speed the game up, but those three cards were the
FIRST thing you put in the deck, and then one or two DU or KR's so you
could steal some VPs if the opportunity arose. Don't TELL me it didn't
work that way, bitches, because again, _I know better_. I've built vote
decks and won with them, and they did just fine at handing beatdowns to
my sequential preys... and I almost never had to play the DU.

-- People should just be including vote defense instead of complaining
about DU/KR.

Hey, guess what; there is no defense other than being able to block the
action, or vote the stuff down. I've already pointed this out in the
past, and I'll point it out again; vote decks have too many advantages
that no other type of deck does.

* Their ousting method starts at +1 stealth.
* Their ousting method cannot have its target changed (Deflection).
* Their ousting method gains them pool (Voter Captivation). Kindred
Spirits and PRE bleed do this to some degree, but not on a par with vote
decks, who can Minion Tap/Voter Cap for the tune of 10 pool per turn if
they do it right. Easy as pie.
* Their ousting method can be directed backwards as defense (see Kindred
Spirits, again), while still trickling forward
* They have access to many "tweaks" to the base game mechanics for free,
where other decks need to spend pool or just don't have access:

= Rumors of Gehenna for free, instead of Parthenon for 2 pool
= Year of Fortune for free, instead of Elder Library for 1 pool
= Political Flux; not available to non-political decks
= Consanguineous Boon; not available to non-political decks
= Praxis: Solomon; not available to non-political decks
= Disputed Territory; not available to anything except superior Dominate
for 2 blood, and even that doesn't get +1 stealth

You think Delaying Tactics is enough? I spit in your face. THREE vote
decks were in the finals at the NAC -- Christian Chenard's winning
bleed-and-vote deck used Con Boons to gain pool (11 pool a pop isn't
good tech? Think again, newb). This compared with one stealth/bleed
deck and one CEL/guns deck. DT was ALL OVER the place, too; someone's
KR got DT'ed three times in my first-round game, because all of us were
packing some. No, I don't think vote is hurting at all, kids. Delaying
Tactics doesn't even make a decent vote deck blink when it comes time to
dish out the ousts, and it only had a SMALL effect against DU. If
people had begun including so many DT that it was impossible to pass the
vote directly, you would've seen Charming Lobby and Cryptic Rider see
more play; of course, you were already seeing Charming Lobby a lot in
order to protect DU from Direct Intervention. Can't DT an autopass
vote, can you?

And when you're cross table and someone is trying to DU to steal your
VP, you can't even block the action. You can't DI, you can't block...
all you can do is DT, and you might not even be able to do that because
of Charming Lobby/Cryptic Rider.

Isn't that some bullshit? Yeah, you know it is.

So all you Chicken Littles out there can just STFU; the sky ain't
falling for vote decks, and it hasn't been for some time. Let's move on
and start discussing how vote decks should adapt themselves to not be
the sit-bloat-and-snipe style that's been so common over the past couple
years (leading directly to timeouts and excessive dealing), and instead
can readapt themselves to be a proper game-winner with a little
resiliency if they happen to get not a perfect seat.

* I'll discuss the myth of bad seating in another post, but frankly,
it's a myth. Too many of the same players win too frequently for it to
be anything else; they aren't ALL lucky, are they?

-- Derek

tuning, maybe consciously leaving areas of vulnerability based on your
perception of the metagame, maybe try to defend against all prevalent
attack forms, but in the end it is luck that determines your opposition.

I disagree.

Consider the following.

5 player table. Nobody has any votes and your neighbors have
no intercept or rush. If you play Law Firm, your +1 stealth and
prince titles will be enough, and you will sweep the table
withouth even blinking once.

If your predator and prey have access to 2nd Traditions, you will
be screwed if you only have 1 stealth. However, if you have a Lasombra
stealth vote deck that easily has 3 or more stealth you can get around
them.

If your predator or prey plays 4-5 intercept block, you need Arika and
her crew to OBF past their block attempts. Not being caught you need
little combat defence, whereas the Law Firm had lots of Majestys and
Prevent. You can use Obedience against rushes and you won't get blocked
anyway, going for the votes at +6 stealth from two stealth cards, with
the option to EI.

How about a deck which has no Intercept but has 7× DT and 10× Deflection
as defence? Arika will be screwed, as she won't be able to play stealth.
Yet Sir Walter and his Oily Bottom Boys would easily swarm past such a
deck.

Metagame determines what makes a good deck and what makes a poor deck.
The good deck is which can exactly use all of its resources to achieve
what it intends to. For example, if your deck plans to do everything at
+3 stealth, you will be very succesful against a deck that tops at +2
Intercept, but will be less effective against someone with no Intercept
or someone with 3.

matter" school comes from, it is simply wrong. If you have 5 players
with roughly equal skill and roughly equal current performance, games
will be dictated by the relative strengths of their decks and their draw.
Sure, many games balance themselves out a bit, and could go any way, but
in the end luck is often a determining factor.

you from gaining VPs by taking your prey away from you.

DTs are not as effective against damage votes as they are against

KRC (especially now without table switching) is likely to just get you
hit by a different damage vote called by the 2nd minion, and then the
same damage vote on the next turn. Not that worthwhile -- therefore it
is actually in the Rush deck's best interest to dump his DTs in favor of

I think... For seat switchers, DT is probably the third best option. You
do not repeat seat switchers during a turn. The card itself is probably
quite valuable in a moment when you want to use it. Therefor I think that
against Seat-Switching the best solution is Direct Intervention. It allows
you to kill that one card and in many cases there won't be another one,
not that turn, not next turn. The second best solution is Vox Domini, as
it costs the same, does basically the same, except it uses up your "Vox
Domini" slot, which could be saved for something really fatal (like being
ousted, or getting one's vampire PTOed). The third best option is Delaying
Tactics.

I think that Delaying Tactics works best against Kine Resources Contested
(predator) or Consanguineous Boon (prey). Those votes are excessively
repeatable and widely used. DI one and another pops up; DT one and you're
in the clear for a turn, even if another 4 copies clog your neighbour's
hand. Parity Shift may be an option, but it is usually only one-shot
anyway. Still, a card and a blood might be worth 5 pool.
